olivia: Heads-up — ran into inconsistent kernel picks on the new DGX nodes after the kernel selector refactor. Some machines are opting into the FP8 codepath even though end-to-end perf is worse for seq_len > 256. Can we discuss a runtime sanity probe and short-circuit flags?

ravi: Ugh, seen this before after driver updates. Two quick things: 1) we need a lightweight probe at service start that microbenchmarks attention matmul for small/med/long seqs (32/128/512) and records best kernel variants. 2) make capability detection explicit (SM, tensor cores, bf16/fp8) — don't trust a single attribute.

jen: Agree. Also we should surface an override env var so infra can bail out quickly: REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL_HINTS (comma list). Useful during rollouts. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: nightly-profiling-summary: a100-dgx-3 - perf delta +8% on token throughput for long-seq workloads after selector refactor. Candidate root cause: fp8 selection on >256 seq.

kai: I'd add that KV cache layout affects effective seq_len for kernel choice — if cache hits reduce active context, the runtime must feed the kernel selector with "effective_seq_len" not the request's total history. We saw mismatches when cached_prefix was counted incorrectly.

olivia: Good catch, kai. That explains why FP8 looked fine on synthetic short contexts but regressed on chat workloads with long histories. We should compute effective_seq = max(new_tokens, tail_window_for_attention) and feed that into the selector.

ravi: For capability detection, use a multi-step check: CUDA device attributes + try a tiny cuBLAS/cuDNN/cuFFT style microkernel call guarded by timeout. Example C-ish probe:```
int major=0, minor=0;
cudaDeviceGetAttribute(&major, cudaDevAttrComputeCapabilityMajor, dev);
cudaDeviceGetAttribute(&minor, cudaDevAttrComputeCapabilityMinor, dev);
int sm = major*10 + minor;
int hasTensorCores = (sm >= 70); // conservative baseline
// then attempt a tiny fp8/bf16 matmul to verify behavior (nonfatal if times out)
```

jen: Nice. Also log both "capability_reported" and "capability_verified" fields so we can distinguish driver lies from real perf. Add a short TTL for probe results (e.g., 24h) and re-run on driver change.

olivia: What about autotuning state? I'm thinking of storing per-node kernel picks in the metadata store with keys: model_hash, sm, driver_build, effective_seq_bucket. Then the selector tries: exact match -> bucket fallback -> global default. We should expire after model update.

kai: Yes. And sequence-length buckets should be 0-64,65-256,257-1024,>1024 since our fused-kernel tradeoffs change at ~256. Also include batch-size bucket since continuous batching changes kernel behavior.

ravi: For quick mitigation during rollout, add a canary rule: if nightly profiler shows regression >5% and capability_verified != true, force fallback to pre-refactor picks for that node. We can wire this to alerting.

jen: Implementation note: kernel selector currently lives in runtime/kernel_picker.cc — patching it to accept an optional probe report struct should be straightforward. I'll add tests that simulate reported-vs-verified mismatches.

perf-bot: probe-run: 1782001200 - node dgx-17 - probe result: SM=80, bf16=true (verified), fp8=reported true, fp8_verified=false, chosen_bucket=257-1024 -> prefer bf16-fused kernel.

olivia: Action items:
- olivia: add startup microbench harness + emit probe report -> target EOD Fri
- ravi: implement capability verification logic + env override REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL_HINTS -> PR next week
- jen: unit+integration tests for selector fallback, TTL semantics -> owner: jen
- kai: KV-cache fix: compute effective_seq_len and update selector callsite -> owner: kai

kai: I'll also add a debug endpoint /runtime/probe that returns last_probe_report so SRE can inspect quickly.

olivia: Thanks all. Let's aim to gate the refactor in canary until probe coverage lands. Posting logs below from a failed canary run for context:```
[2026-03-10 04:12:36] node dgx-17 selected kernel: attention_fp8_fused
[2026-03-10 04:12:36] probe_effective_seq=512, reported_fp8=true, fp8_verified=false
[2026-03-10 04:12:36] throughput_before=1200 tokens/s, after=1100 tokens/s (−8%)
```

ravi: Perfect. I'll carve out the env var + quick override API so infra can flip it without a restart.

jen: Will add the regression alert to the perf dashboard and a playbook snippet for rollback.

olivia: Excellent. We'll sync tomorrow in the runtime standup. :calendar:
